problem: No simulator or dataset supports training RL agents for Outdoor Micro-Navigation (OMN): the last few metres of pedestrian navigation to a specific street address or door. Street-View environments such as StreetLearn and 'Learning to Navigate in Cities without a Map' use vehicle-mounted, low-resolution imagery (1664x832) with nodes about 10 m apart and block-sized goals. They lack door, house-number and street-sign annotations, and indoor VLN simulators do not cover the domain.
motivation: Interviews and market research with Blind and Visually Impaired (BVI) people, specialists and 12 app developers showed that finding the exact entrance near a destination is a major unsolved problem. People pay over $1/min for human-in-the-loop services (Aira, BeMyEyes) because GPS apps such as Google Maps get them only close to the goal. Sighted humans solve the task by fusing vision, scene text (house numbers, street signs) and GPS, so the thesis asks whether a DRL agent can learn to do the same.
key_idea: Build pedestrian-perspective navigation environments (Grid Street/Grid City gridworlds and SEVN, a graph of 4,988 densely annotated 360° sidewalk panoramas at 1 node/m) and train a PPO agent that tiles GPS, house-number and street-sign encodings into extra image channels, so one CNN fuses all modalities to navigate to a target door.
insight: Every modality matters, and they are complementary. On SEVN Small, image-only reaches 57% SR, adding GT scene text gives 58.2% (NoGPS), and adding GPS on top gives 74.9% (AllObs). Removing images collapses the policy to 0.8%, worse than a random walk (5.7%), so even 84x84 images are essential. However, the policies memorise the training region rather than learning general concepts such as house-number ordering: the Small-trained model gets 1.0% SR on the Large region, and a model trained on Large for 20M frames reaches only 21.1% SR there. The gridworld chapter shows the same weakness: sparse-reward PPO without a curriculum reaches only about 10% of optimal reward on Static Grid City, a distance-ordered curriculum is needed, domain randomization prevents learning even the first goal, and frame-stacking (1/8/16) has no effect. In the noisy-GPS ablation, large noise (25/100 m) makes AllObs perform like NoGPS, while small noise has little effect.
method: Grid Street / Grid City (gym-minigrid): partially observable static gridworlds with houses, monotone odd/even house numbers, street signs and lava roads. The agent sees a 5x5x3 egocentric view and a language instruction ('go to street 0 house 3'), acts with {left, right, forward, done}, and receives a sparse γ^i reward only on a correct 'done'.

Gridworld agent: a 3-layer CNN encodes the observation and a GRU encodes the instruction. The two embeddings are concatenated into shared actor/critic heads (2 FC + tanh), trained with PPO (clip 0.2, 32 processes x 128 steps) and no recurrence (frame-stacking tried instead). A curriculum adds the next-farthest goal once success exceeds 95% in an update batch; a domain-randomized variant is also tested.

SEVN dataset/simulator: Vuze+ 360° video of about 6.3 km of Little Italy (Montreal) sidewalks, localised with ORB-SLAM2 and sparsified to 1 node/m. It has 4,988 panoramas (3840x1280) with hand-labelled door polygons, house-number and street-sign boxes plus transcriptions, split into Large (3,831) and Small (1,157). It is an OpenAI Gym env running at 400-800 FPS with an oracle shortest-path planner (NetworkX).

SEVN task suite: 8 tasks built on dense shaped reward (+1/-1 per node closer/farther; +0.1/-0.2 for turns toward/away from the correct heading). Variants cover modality ablations (AllObs/NoImg/NoGPS/ImgOnly), Intersection crossing, CostlyTxt (a 'read' action costing -0.2), Sparse (requires 'done' with the door in view) and Explorer (+1 per house number seen). Success means occupying the goal node with the target door fully inside the FOV.

Observations: an 84x84 RGB crop (135° FOV) of a low-res panorama; high-res 1280x1280 is optional. Scene text comes from ground-truth labels fully contained in the FOV: house numbers as four one-hot(10) digits, up to 3 stacked, and street names as one-hot(11). Simulated GPS gives absolute and relative goal coordinates scaled to [-1,1].

Multi-modal fusion policy: each non-image modality vector is tiled/padded into a (1,w,w) plane and appended to the RGB channels, giving an (8,w,w) tensor. Missing modalities are zero-filled. The tensor passes through 3 conv layers and a 256-unit dense layer (ReLU) to an action softmax, plus a value head. Training uses PPO with Atari hyperparameters except lr 3e-4 and 2M frames.

setting.backbone: small 3-layer CNN + 256-d dense actor-critic (trained from scratch with PPO); gridworld variant adds a GRU instruction encoder
setting.training_data: RL experience in SEVN Small split (1,157 panoramas, 116 goal doors), 2M frames per seed, 10 seeds; a Large-split model is trained for 20M frames; gridworld agents trained 1M frames (one run 40M) in Grid Street/City
setting.observation: egocentric 84x84 RGB crop (135° FOV) of a 360° panorama + ground-truth visible scene text (house numbers, street names, one-hot) + simulated GPS goal offset / absolute goal coordinates
setting.action_space: discrete panorama-graph moves: slight turns ±22.5°, sharp turns ±67.5°, forward to the neighbour node nearest the heading (~1 m spacing); optional 'read' and 'done' actions in some tasks
setting.simulator: SEVN (OpenAI Gym, real sidewalk panoramas of Little Italy, Montreal); Grid Street / Grid City (gym-minigrid)
setting.privileged: ground-truth scene-text annotations (house numbers / street signs in FOV) fed as observations instead of OCR; noise-free simulated GPS goal offset (except in the noisy-GPS ablation); dense shaped reward computed from the oracle during training

numbers_note: SEVN has no official val/test splits; 'val-seen' marks train=eval on the same region and 'val-unseen' marks the cross-region evaluation (Small→Large). Only tasks 1-4 (modality ablations) are reported numerically; the Intersection, CostlyTxt, Sparse and Explorer tasks have no results. The noisy-GPS ablation and all Grid Street/Grid City experiments are shown only as training-curve figures. Text statements are 'about 0.2' average reward, >95% success on 5 goals after 1M frames with the curriculum, and up to 9 goals after 40M frames. Oracle (100% SR, 80.8 steps) and Random (5.7% SR) are reference rows, not own methods. There are internal inconsistencies: FOV is stated as 140° and 135°, and Small→Large SR is 1.4% in the text vs 1.0% in Table 4.5.
results: On SEVN Small, the full-modality AllObs PPO agent reaches 74.9% (±7.8) SR, with the best seed at 85%, and uses 113.7 steps on average. The oracle needs 80.8 steps at 100% SR, and a random walk gets 5.7%. It clearly beats its own modality ablations: NoGPS 58.2%, ImgOnly 57%, NoImg 0.8%. Generalization to unseen streets fails: the Small-trained model gets 1.0% SR on Large, and even training on Large for 20M frames yields only 21.1%. In the gridworlds, sparse-reward PPO needs a curriculum to master a handful of goals, and it fails entirely under domain randomization.
limitations: Uses ground-truth hand-labelled scene text and exact simulated GPS rather than OCR or real GPS. Only tasks 1-4 are reported, with no results on the Intersection, Sparse, CostlyTxt or Explorer tasks.
Policies do not generalize beyond the training region (1.0% SR Small→Large; 21.1% even when trained on Large), and the dataset is small (one neighbourhood, 116 goals in Small).
Simulation only: a static panorama graph with no dynamic obstacles or off-sidewalk path planning, no real-device/BVI user testing, and simple no-memory CNN policies trained with only 2M frames.
